Imprudent

/im-PROO-dent/ — emphasis on PROO, rhymes with prudent · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

An action that is imprudent is unwise or careless, taken without properly thinking through the consequences.

Spending the whole allowance on candy was an imprudent choice.

Worked Example

His imprudent decision to drop out of school left him struggling to find work.

Imprudent is more precise than 'foolish' here because it captures not just lack of wisdom but specifically the failure to think through the consequences of his choice — he didn't foresee how much he would struggle.

How Imprudent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

hasty

hasty: done too quickly, without enough thought

reckless

reckless: ignoring obvious danger or serious consequences

careless

careless: failing to give proper thought or attention

Antonyms

prudent

prudent: wise and cautious about future consequences

judicious

judicious: showing careful, sensible, well-reasoned judgment

How Strong Is It? — hasty → reckless → foolish → imprudent

hasty vs. imprudent

hasty vs. imprudent: Hasty is slightly weaker than imprudent: a hasty choice is merely rushed, while an imprudent one ignores consequences that a wise person would have weighed.

reckless vs. imprudent

reckless vs. imprudent: Reckless is stronger than imprudent: an imprudent decision overlooks the consequences, but a reckless one charges ahead despite clear and serious danger.

foolish vs. imprudent

foolish vs. imprudent: Foolish is the strongest word on this scale, beyond imprudent: an imprudent act shows poor planning, while a foolish one defies common sense altogether.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — im- (in-)

Prefix — im- (in-): not, opposite of (Latin)

Root — prud- (providens)

Root — prud- (providens): seeing ahead, foreseeing, wise (Latin)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: adjective ending: being in a state (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Im- means 'not,' and prudent traces to Latin providens, 'seeing ahead' (a contraction of pro- 'before' + videre 'to see'): an imprudent action is taken by someone not looking ahead at the consequences.

Use the root in a new word: prudent

Use the root in a new word: prudent: Drop the im- and you get prudent: a prudent person 'sees ahead' and plans for consequences — exactly what an imprudent person fails to do.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Imprudent describes a failure of judgment that should have been foreseen. Use it when someone makes a major choice that was unwise in an obvious way. For a single careless moment, 'careless' is clearer; for an action done with reckless defiance, 'reckless' fits better.
